intent: To illustrate the dramatic growth of the global population, reaching record levels by 2014.

units.meaning: By 2014, world population reached 8.00 billion, the highest/record value in the series.

basis.note: Final year in table; also max value because 2010-2014 all equal 8.00B.

accepted_routes: By 2014, world population was 8.00 billion, the highest in the dataset.
The 2014 population reached 8 billion, a record level in this series.
The final chart value is 8.00B in 2014, the all-time high shown.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The final point/area at 2014 must align with 8.00B on the y-axis, and the chart must make clear this is the top/record level.
units.temporal_anchor: The 'global population is at an all-time high' clause.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly mark 2014 as the record/endpoint value of 8.00B?

units.meaning: World population grew dramatically from 1.02 billion in 1800 to 8.00 billion in 2014, an increase of 6.98 billion, or about 7.8 times.
accepted_routes: World population rose from 1.02B in 1800 to 8.00B in 2014, an increase of 6.98B.
It grew almost eightfold over the period, adding about 7 billion people.
From 1800 to 2014, population increased by roughly 684%, or 7.8x.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both the 1800 start value (1.02B) and the 2014 endpoint (8.00B) must be visible or directly labeled, with the connecting growth/area making the change apparent.
units.temporal_anchor: The 'global population' clause; if narration expands, this should lead into the 'at an all-time high' statement.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the full 1800-to-2014 growth, or is showing the endpoint alone sufficient?

units.meaning: The world population trend is upward over 1800-2014; the table values never decrease from year to year.

basis.note: Series end; higher than all prior values.

accepted_routes: World population increases over time from 1800 to 2014.
The population line trends upward throughout the period.
The annual series is non-decreasing and ends much higher than it begins.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The animated line/area must rise from left to right across the 1800-2014 x-axis, not show a decline.
units.reviewer_question: Must the animation visibly establish an upward trend, or is the start-to-end change enough?

units.meaning: World population first reached 8.00 billion in 2010 and stayed at 8.00 billion through 2014.
accepted_routes: Population first hit 8 billion in 2010 and remained at 8.00B through 2014.
The 8B threshold is reached by 2010 and held to 2014.
World population crossed the 8B mark between 2009 and 2010.
units.visual_evidence_rule: An 8B gridline or callout should show the crossing at 2010 and the flat 8.00B level through 2014.
units.temporal_anchor: The 'at an all-time high' clause, if the video specifies when the high was first reached.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video mark the first 8B crossing in 2010, or only the 2014 record endpoint?

units.meaning: Most of the population growth was recent: the 1900-2014 increase was 6.10 billion, compared with 0.88 billion from 1800 to 1900, about 6.9 times larger.
accepted_routes: From 1900 to 2014, population rose by 6.10B, versus only 0.88B from 1800 to 1900.
Recent growth dominates: the post-1900 increase was about 7 times the 19th-century increase.
Most of the total increase came after 1900, adding 6.1B compared with 0.9B before.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart or annotation must distinguish the 1800-1900 segment from the 1900-2014 segment, or label the two increases.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video quantify the acceleration by comparing 1800-1900 with 1900-2014?

optional_valid: World population more than quadrupled from 1900 (1.90B) to 2014 (8.00B): 8.00 / 1.90 = 4.21x.
Population first passed 6 billion between 1986 (5.90B) and 1987 (6.03B).
Population first passed 7 billion between 1998 (6.98B) and 1999 (7.12B).
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that war going out of fashion caused population growth.
Claims about years before 1800 or after 2014.
Treating relative_value as a share, percentage, or absolute population size.
Saying population first hit 8 billion only in 2014; the table shows 8.00B from 2010 through 2014.
Saying population doubled from 1800 to 2014; the table implies about a 7.8x rise.
notes: The core G1 should include the 1800-to-2014 growth and the 2014 record value; the first 8B crossing and century acceleration are valid optional refinements. All cited numbers are table cells or simple differences/ratios.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
